item.title: Dispersive decay for the modified Benjamin-Ono equation with small data
item.description: arXiv:2611.17444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the modified Benjamin-Ono equation for small, localized initial data where no solitons arise, and prove a dispersive estimate. Unlike the standard Benjamin-Ono equation, the modified version is not known to be completely integrable, so we cannot rely on integrable systems tools. First, to manage the nonlocal Hilbert transform in the linear part of the equation, we project the equation to positive and negative frequencies. We then combine wave packet testing of Ifrim-Tataru, the Klainerman-Sobolev vector field method, and a bootstrap argument.
item.dc:creator: Allison Byars

item.title: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $\Gamma$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
item.description: arXiv:2611.17543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $\Gamma$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $\Gamma$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $\beta_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile. The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $\beta_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Di Fratta, Valeriy V. Slastikov

item.title: Scattering for cubic and Yukawa--Hartree Dirac equations wiith polynomially decaying spacetime metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.17593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study massive Dirac equations in three space dimensions with small, time-dependent perturbations of the principal coefficients and decaying zeroth-order matrix terms. The principal perturbation and its spatial derivatives decay polynomially at rate $\rho>7/2$, and its first time derivative has one additional inverse spatial power. We prove small-data global well-posedness and scattering for local cubic nonlinearities in $H^s$, $s>1+5/(2(\rho-1))$, and for Yukawa--Hartree nonlinearities in $H^s$, $s>1/2+5/(2(\rho-1))$. The argument retains the coupling between the metric-adapted positive and negative branches. Its main ingredients are a time-independent modified energy, a weighted estimate controlling the full massive low-frequency component, and frequency-dependent spatial cutoffs. The operator class contains the geometric Dirac Hamiltonian of a synchronous spacetime metric with its full spin connection. No second time derivative, temporal integrability, or asymptotic stationarity is assumed. Scattering is formulated relative to the exact nonautonomous linear evolution.
item.dc:creator: Yonggeun Cho

item.title: The retarded interaction and non-scattering for 3D Maxwell--Dirac system
item.description: arXiv:2611.17595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an a priori obstruction to linear scattering for the massive Maxwell--Dirac system in three space dimensions. A global solution with nonzero charge cannot scatter linearly in $L^2$ if its full and homogeneous potentials are $O(t^{-1})$, and the homogeneous potential is $o(t^{-1})$ in compact timelike cones. No nonlinear asymptotic expansion is assumed in this non-scattering theorem. We also identify the exact leading interaction when the nonlinear current approaches a free Dirac current in $L^1$. Its coefficient is a positive quadratic form in the velocity density and is bounded below by the square of the charge divided by $4\pi$. The proof uses free Dirac asymptotics and an estimate for retarded source errors after pairing with a smooth free current. The main arguments, including the oscillatory retarded interaction, are proved here. Global existence and the required nonlinear decay remain separate inputs; a small-data application to existing theory is stated explicitly as such.
item.dc:creator: Yonggeun Cho, Kiyeon Lee

item.title: Counterexamples to the clamped-plate eigenvalue ratio conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.17606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ashbaugh in 1999 conjectures that the ball maximizes the ratio of the second to the first eigenvalue for the vibrating clamped-plate problem. We disprove this conjecture by constructing smooth connected domains in every dimension $d\ge2$. The construction starts with an interior sphere on which the displacement is required to vanish. The first two eigenvalues have the same relative increase at first order, but the second increases more at second order. This gives a strict increase of their ratio, which survives approximation of the sphere by finitely many codimension-two supports and their replacement by smooth holes. We identify the limiting Sobolev spaces through trace estimates and logarithmic cutoffs, and use the geometric construction for the buckling problem to obtain connected perforated domains.
item.dc:creator: Guowei Dai, Yingxin Sun, Yong Zhang

item.title: Pseudo-profiles for vectorial Allen-Cahn systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.17611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of the present paper is to present a new type of solutions to the elliptic vectorial Allen-Cahn system of equations. Its main feature is that in the classical rescaling its asymptotics do not follow the rule of balance of energies, which is crucial in the analysis of the asymptotics for the scalar problem.
item.dc:creator: Fabrice Bethuel, Dongheng Liu, Ramon Oliver Bonafoux

item.title: Dynamics of a single 3D vortex ring
item.description:
arXiv:2611.17635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flow without swirl originating from a circular vortex ring. For each fixed $s\in(0,1)$ and sufficiently large circulation Reynolds number $\Gamma/
u$, we prove that, on the time scale $t\lesssim T_{m adv}(\Gamma/
u)^{s}$, the vorticity $\omega_	heta$ is approximated by a traveling wave solution featuring a Gaussian-type core with scale $O(\sqrt{
u t})$, whose off-axis distance remains constant and which continuously translates along the axial direction. In particular, the leading-order axial translation velocity is given by the Kelvin-Saffman formula. The proof relies on the approximation and Arnold energy framework of Gallay and \v{S}ver'ak \cite{GS2024}. We modify the weight used in \cite{GS2024} and estimate the relative-vorticity error to obtain favorable boundary dissipation at the symmetry axis and close the energy estimate.
item.dc:creator: Ping Zhang, Yibin Zhang

item.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.17640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets, including disconnected sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.
item.dc:creator: Carrie Clark, Richard S. Laugesen

item.title: Strong solutions to the Cahn--Hilliard--Darcy--Forchheimer system for incompressible two-phase flows with a soluble surfactant
item.description: arXiv:2611.17668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a diffuse-interface model for incompressible viscous two-phase flows with a soluble surfactant in a bounded porous medium in two or three dimensions. The resulting system consists of a Darcy--Forchheimer equation for the seepage velocity $\bm{u}$ coupled with two Cahn--Hilliard equations, one for the difference in volume fractions of the two fluids denoted by $\phi$, and the other for the local concentration of the surfactant $\psi$. In the general scenario of non-constant coefficients and mobilities, we establish the existence of a local (resp. global) strong solution in three (resp. two) dimensions to the corresponding initial-boundary value problem with the no-flux boundary conditions for the phase-field variables and chemical potentials and a no-penetration condition for the velocity. In the case of constant coefficients in the Darcy--Forchheimer equation and constant mobilities in the Cahn--Hilliard equations, with a suitably large Forchheimer exponent, we establish the existence of a global strong solution in three dimensions. Furthermore, using the {\L}ojasiewicz--Simon approach, we prove the global existence of a unique strong solution when the initial data are sufficiently close to a local energy minimizer of the free energy.
item.dc:creator: Maurizio Grasselli, Bohan Ouyang, Hao Wu

item.title: Co-rotating and traveling asymmetric vortex sheets for the planar Euler equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.17687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to construct co-rotating and traveling vortex sheet pairs with asymmetric configurations for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation. The vorticity of these solutions is concentrated on two small closed curves of different sizes, which carry vortex sheets of different circulations and either rotate uniformly about their centroid or translate with constant speed. The proof relies on the Birkhoff--Rott formulation of the problem and on the implicit function theorem at the point vortex pairs.
item.dc:creator: Edison Cuba

item.title: The Dirichlet Problem for Quaternionic $k$-Hessian Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for quaternionic $k$-Hessian equations on smooth bounded domains. For a smooth positive density $f(q,z)$ satisfying $f_z\ge0$, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth admissible solution whenever a smooth admissible subsolution with the prescribed boundary values exists. The proof extends the quaternionic Monge--Amp\`ere subsolution method to $2\le k<n$ through boundary second derivative estimates. We also construct subsolutions on strictly quaternionic $(k-1)$-convex domains and characterize smooth solvability for constant boundary values.
item.dc:creator: Xi-Nan Ma, Yang Zhou, Jingyong Zhu

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions to semilinear elliptic problems on the exterior of a unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem \begin{equation}\notag \begin{cases} - \Delta u &= \lambda K(x) f(u) \hspace{.1cm} \mbox { in } B_1 ^c, \\ u(x)&=0 \hspace{1.5cm} \mbox { on } \partial B_1, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\lambda$ is a positive parameter, $B_1^c:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:|x|>1\}$ is the exterior of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $K:B_1^c\rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a $C^1$ radial function and $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a $C^1$ concave function which is sublinear at infinity such that $f(0)<0$. We establish the existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions for large values of parameter $\lambda$. Moreover, we prove certain qualitative properties of nonnegative radial solutions for a class of problems in dimension 2. In contrast to the case $n\geq3$, where positive solutions decay to zero at infinity, we prove that non negative solutions are positive, radially increasing with the limit existing at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Ameerraja Ansari, Lakshmi Sankar

item.title: Existence and regularity for a non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation with a confining potential
item.description: arXiv:2611.18004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation $\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1-|Du|^2})-V(x)u+|u|^{p-2}u=0$ in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\ge3$ and $2<p<2^*=2N/(N-2)$. For a $C^1$ potential satisfying $\inf V>0$, $V(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and $|x\cdot\nabla V(x)|\le C_DV(x)$ with $0\le C_D<p-2$, we prove the existence of a positive classical solution and infinitely many distinct nontrivial classical solutions. The argument combines the nonsmooth monotonicity trick with compactness induced by the confining potential. A Pohozaev-type identity yields uniform bounds for parameter-dependent critical points. A local minimization characterization identifies these critical points with weak solutions and establishes strict spacelikeness. Local Schauder estimates then give $C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity. All the solutions belong to the natural energy space $H_V^1(\mathbb R^N)$ and satisfy $|Du|<1$.
item.dc:creator: Fan Yang, Chengxiang Zhang

item.title: Local well-posedness for the Novikov-Veselov equation at subcritical regularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.18046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish local well-posedness of the Novikov--Veselov equation (NV), at every fixed value of the energy parameter, for initial data in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ in the entire subcritical Sobolev range $s>-1$. The argument is perturbative and does not invoke the integrable structure, instead adapting the strategy in our previous work on KdV (2026). An infinite normal-form expansion indexed by binary trees is combined with a gauge transform that bypasses the obstructions in the associate bilinear estimate, and the resulting gauged equation -- carrying nonlinear contributions of every order -- is closed by a contraction in a Fourier restriction space. The analytic engine is a family of frequency-restricted multilinear bounds, supported by a detailed description of the two-dimensional resonance geometry attached to (NV).
item.dc:creator: Andreia Chapouto, Sim\~ao Correia, Jo\~ao Pedro Ramos

item.title: Stochastic Nonlocal Conservation Laws with L\'evy Noise: Stability, BV Estimates, and Vanishing Viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2611.18051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study one-dimensional stochastic nonlocal conservation laws with a convolution-type interaction field, driven by multiplicative Brownian noise and compensated Poisson random measures. The nonlocal operator modifies the classical entropy structure, while the jump noise produces nonlinear correction terms in the entropy inequality. We introduce a notion of stochastic entropy solution and establish an $L^1$-stability estimate using spatial doubling of variables and the It\^o--L\'evy formula. This yields uniqueness in the vanishing-viscosity class and, under additional bounds, a localized Cauchy estimate of order $\sqrt{\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}$. Existence is obtained by vanishing viscosity: we construct the viscous solutions through a Faedo--Galerkin scheme and derive viscosity-uniform $L^1$ and localized $BV$ estimates, which allow us to pass to the limit and obtain a spatially $BV$ stochastic entropy solution.
item.dc:creator: Aekta Aggarwal, Debopriya Mukherjee, Akash Ashirbad Panda

item.title: Stochastic inverse source problem in inhomogeneous media: far-field statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.18070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is concerned with an inverse random source problem for the stochastic Helmholtz equation in a known three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is driven by spatial white noise. We seek to recover its mean and strength from the mean and cross-frequency covariance of the far-field pattern. For a smooth nontrapping wave speed, we use the spectral measure of the acoustic operator to relate the far-field data to the source statistics. Under a priori regularity bounds, this relation gives conditional stability for the source mean and the source strength. We derive explicit reconstruction formulas for both quantities and bound the errors due to frequency truncation and data perturbations. We also obtain mean-square error bounds for reconstructions from finitely many independent experiments. Numerical experiments illustrate the reconstruction accuracy and the effects of bandwidth and sample size.
item.dc:creator: Dong Qiu, Xiang Xu, Yue Zhao

item.title: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.18151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the unforced Euler equations, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity within the class of axisymmetric flows without swirl, whose solution blows up in finite time. The initial vorticity belongs simultaneously to every H\"older space $C^\alpha$, $\alpha<1/3$. This is sharp given that global regularity is known when $\alpha=1/3$ in the case of axisymmetric flows without swirl. Previous constructions by Shkoller \cite{Shk26}, Chen \cite{Chen26I,Chen26II}, and Shao--Wei--Zhang--Zhang \cite{SWZZ26} establish blow-up for each prescribed exponent $\alpha$ in the same sharp range. Our construction achieves simultaneous membership in all these spaces. In addition, our construction is short. Our proof uses multiscale initial data, in the spirit of Kim--Jeong~\cite{KJ22}, C\'ordoba--Mart\'inez-Zoroa--Zheng~\cite{CMZZ25}, and Bang--Cheskidov~\cite{BC26}. The blow-up mechanism is a forward cascade through successively smaller scales. A main difficulty in approaching the critical exponent $1/3$ is caused by large self-deformation. Our main idea to overcome this difficulty is to obtain a lower bound for strain at the stationary non-smooth point by using angular redistribution. A related outstanding open problem is to establish an unforced Euler blow-up from smooth data in the case of axisymmetric flows with swirl. A recent multiscale construction by OpenAI for the unforced Euler equations is, however, non-axisymmetric. Although we work in the no-swirl class, the axisymmetric multiscale mechanism developed here may offer a possible route toward the still-open problem of axisymmetric smooth blow-up.
item.dc:creator: Jeaheang Bang, Alexey Cheskidov

item.title: The Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth
item.description: arXiv:2611.18203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth. For the full water wave system, we derive an explicit instability index and rigorously classify its sign throughout the depth-vorticity plane. With gravitational acceleration and carrier wavenumber normalized to one, we identify a unique minimum depth $h_{\text{crit}}\approx1.36271$, below which Benjamin-Feir instability is absent for every vorticity. Above this depth, two vorticity thresholds delimit the unstable regime, outside of which the spectrum near the origin remains purely imaginary for all small Floquet exponents. In particular, at each fixed finite depth, constant vorticity of sufficiently large magnitude suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability. Moreover, any constant vorticity $\gamma\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$ suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability at every finite depth. The proof combines Hamiltonian spectral perturbation theory, symbolic computations, and formal verification in Rocq. Away from the transition set, our results rigorously confirm the stability criterion predicted by the nonlinear Schr\"odinger approximation of Thomas, Kharif, and Manna.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Chen, Huy Q. Nguyen

item.title: Optimal polynomial decay and nonlinear stabilization for an indirectly damped wave-MGT system
item.description: arXiv:2611.18234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a conservative wave equation coupled to a dissipative Moore--Gibson--Thompson equation by a zero-order interaction that is symmetric in augmented variables. A general modal proposition relates the exact resolvent and semigroup asymptotic constants through an asymptotically unitary diagonalization. Its application to this system yields the optimal fourth-order resolvent estimate and the exact linear decay constants. These estimates lead to nonlinear stabilization from small regular initial data. On smooth bounded domains, a weighted composition estimate that accommodates a singular third derivative of the source at zero gives the optimal state rate $t^{-3/4}$ and energy rate $t^{-3/2}$ for power and logarithmic sources. In dimension three, the result includes $f(u)=|u|^q u$ with $3/2<q<2$ and $f(u)=|u|^{\gamma-2}u\log|u|$ with $7/2<\gamma<4$, within the source ranges of the companion general-source theory. Dimension-dependent extensions hold through dimension seven in the same data space, and in arbitrary dimension with higher regularity and a higher order of vanishing at zero. A lower-regularity graph-norm theorem and a conditional transfer theorem for general sources are also proved. Each nonlinear small-data decay exponent is optimal among uniform estimates with the stated dependence on the initial-data norm.
item.dc:creator: Tae Gab Ha

item.title: Simultaneous recovery of elastic and viscous coefficients in a Kelvin-Voigt equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.18242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the simultaneous recovery of a spatially dependent elastic coefficient and a time- and space-dependent viscosity coefficient in a scalar Kelvin-Voigt equation. We prove that the displacement-to-traction map over any fixed time interval uniquely determines both coefficients, provided that the Riemannian metric induced by the viscosity is simple at each time. In the velocity formulation, the elastic term gives rise to a Volterra memory term involving second-order spatial derivatives, with a corresponding memory contribution to the boundary traction. We first determine all normal derivatives of both coefficients at the boundary using highly oscillatory boundary data. We then construct exact parabolic exponential solutions in the presence of memory and determine the viscosity by boundary rigidity. With the viscosity determined, an approximate identity argument reduces recovery of the elastic coefficient to injectivity of the scalar geodesic ray transform. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate a regularized finite-dimensional reconstruction of both coefficients from finitely many moments of the displacement-to-traction map.
item.dc:creator: Dong Qiu, Song-Ren Fu, Yeqiong Ye, Ting Zhou

item.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.18265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \bar{\sigma}_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)-h, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+\delta, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_\mu}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cot\theta, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<\theta\le\pi/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_\mu\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<\theta<\pi$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.
item.dc:creator: Dongjing Ma, Peihe Wang, Hua Zhu

item.title: Inverse energy transfer for 2D Navier--Stokes near a self-similar vortex collapse
item.description: arXiv:2611.18269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove inverse energy transfer for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse, confirming the 1979 prediction of Novikov and Sedov. Nonlinear interactions transfer kinetic energy from high to low frequencies over a common time interval that shrinks to the collapse time as the viscosity tends to zero. We prove that the net nonlinear transfer over this interval converges to the same positive constant across an expanding range of frequency cutoffs, with quantitative error bounds uniform in the cutoff.
item.dc:creator: Trinh T. Nguyen

item.title: Nondegeneracy of the bubble for a fourth-order Liouville boundary problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.18277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the nondegeneracy of the bubble for \[ \Delta^2u=0\quad \text{in }\mathbb R^4_+,\qquad \partial_tu=0,\quad \partial_t\Delta u=e^{24\pi^2u} \quad \text{on }\partial\mathbb R^4_+. \] Using Fourier analysis, stereographic projection and a removable-singularity argument, we classify the weighted $L^2$ boundary kernel without assuming boundedness of the boundary solution. This determines the bounded half-space kernel. Both kernels are generated by dilation and tangential translations. We further obtain sharp estimates for the projected spherical inverse.
item.dc:creator: Jiaoping Chen, Wenjing Chen, Shengbing Deng

item.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
item.description:
arXiv:2611.18287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<	heta<\pi/2$, we consider \[ \sigma_k(
abla^2h+h\sigma) = f(\xi)h^{p-1} rac{ho^{k+1}}{\varphi(ho)}, \qquad ho=(h^2+|
abla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $
abla_\mu h=\cot	heta\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.
item.dc:creator: Dongjing Ma, Qiqi Zhang, Hua Zhu

item.title: On the dynamics of N classical particles interacting with a complex environment
item.description: arXiv:2611.18292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interactions of a particle with its environment eventually lead to the damping of its motion. This phenomenom is well understood when considering a single particle exchanging energy with the environment. The situation is definitely more complex when many particles are considered: the energy dissipation mechanisms are not clear whenever particles create a common well in which they keep interacting. In this framework, we identify the equilibrium solutions, that consist in clusters of particles at rest, and we establish their spectral stability. We show that the mean position/velocity pair is damped exponentially fast at the linearized level. Coming back to the non linear problem, we can show, at least in some simplified cases, that the dissipation mechanisms also involve far slower rates, that explain the difficulty in observing the relaxation behavior on the individual trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Thierry Goudon (LJAD), Bruno Marcos (LJAD), Thomas Oudeville (LJAD), Simona Rota Nodari (LJAD, IUF)

item.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.18299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\bar\sigma_k(\nabla^2h+h\sigma)=f, \qquad \nabla_\mu h=\cot\theta\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+\delta, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.
item.dc:creator: Hua Zhu

item.title: Quantitative high-contrast homogenisation of composite media with highly anisotropic fibres
item.description: arXiv:2611.18354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work concerns a non-uniformly elliptic second-order differential operator with periodic coefficients that describes a composite medium formed by a periodic array of highly anisotropic cylindrical fibres set in an isotropic matrix. The ratio of transverse to axial conductivity in the fibres is linked to the period of the coefficients through a `critical' high-contrast scaling, and the axial conductivity is allowed to vary along the fibres. As the period $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, ellipticity degenerates in the directions transverse to the fibres. We are concerned with the resolvent of this operator in the small-$\varepsilon$ limit. For fibres with constant axial conductivity, the two-scale limit of such problems was identified by Cherednichenko, Smyshlyaev and Zhikov (Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh: Section A Mathematics 136(1), 87--114 (2006)), and a full two-scale asymptotic expansion, with remainder estimates for smooth right-hand sides, was constructed by Cherednichenko (Asymptotic Analysis 49(1--2), 39--59 (2006)). In the non-constant axial conductivity setting, considered here, we approximate the resolvent in terms of the two-scale limit operator and prove that the error is order $\varepsilon$ in the operator norm, uniformly over right-hand sides in the unit ball of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$; we also obtain order-$\varepsilon$ estimates for the reciprocals of the spectral band functions. This work builds on results announced, without proof, for fibres with circular cross-section in Cooper and Kamotski (Direct and Inverse Problems with Applications: Extended Abstracts of the 2024 GAP Center Summer School, pp.~69--75, Birkh\"auser (2026)).
item.dc:creator: Shane Cooper, Ilia Kamotski

item.title: Normalized ground state solutions to the nonlinear Born--Infeld problem
item.dc:creator: Jaros\law Mederski, Xiangjian Zeng

item.title: The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells
item.description: arXiv:2611.18368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.
item.dc:creator: Kaixin Deng, Senping Luo

item.title: Thresholds of the Polya Szego inequality for the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.18425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish three surprising features of the Polya Szego principle for the full signed energy of the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian. First, the energy doesn't not decrease under rearrangement for all admissible functions. Second, the sharp threshold for Polarization and Schwarz rearrangements are different. Third, for Steiner rearrangement, the threshold in 1 dimension and N dimensions is not the same. Additionally the dimension doesn't appear in the formula.
item.dc:creator: Hichem Hajaiej

item.title: Maxwell's equations with thin wires in critical scaling
item.description: arXiv:2611.18446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive effective equations for a situation in which electromagnetic waves hit an array of very thin wires. We study two cases, perfectly conducting wires and highly conducting wires, and investigate in both the critical scaling of the parameters. The electric field $E^\eta$ and the magnetic field $H^\eta$ satisfy the time-harmonic Maxwell equations, and the small parameter $\eta>0$ is the spacing of the wires. A non-critical scaling of the wires implies either that the wires have no effect or that the tangential component of the limiting electric field in the direction of the wires vanishes along the effective interface. In the critical scaling, we observe an interesting effect: The wires act as oscillators and there is a relation between the electric field in longitudinal direction and the jump of the magnetic field in transversal direction involving second derivatives of a flux quantity.
item.dc:creator: Ben Schweizer, David Wiedemann

item.title: Multiplicity of Positive Solutions for Singular Anisotropic Elliptic Equations with Variable Exponents
item.description: arXiv:2611.18488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study anisotropic elliptic Dirichlet problems with variable exponents, singular nonlinearities, and subcritical superlinear reactions. Our contribution is a direct variational construction that combines Nehari geometry and fibering maps without requiring global differentiability of the singular energy, and the result establishes the existence of two positive weak solutions for sufficiently small \(\lambda\), distinguished by their energy signs.
item.dc:creator: Ali Akbar Esmailnejad, Somayeh Khademloo, Seyyed Hashem Rasouli

item.title: Sharp nonuniqueness for the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system
item.description: arXiv:2611.18554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system on $\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. For smooth data and every $p<2$, $q<\infty$, we construct infinitely many weak solutions with velocity in $L^p_tL^\infty\cap L^1_tW^{1,q}$ and bounded, renormalized distribution function; infinitely many of them violate the energy inequality. For smooth velocity data, weak solutions with velocity in $L^2_tL^\infty$ are unique, so the result is sharp at the endpoint of the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin scale. The fluid carries the nonuniqueness, through the convex integration scheme of Cheskidov and Luo, and the kinetic equation is solved exactly. The main new difficulty is the memory of the particles: the kinetic state at time $t$ depends on the whole past of the velocity, so a modification on a short interval changes the system at all later times. We overcome it by a causal gluing, carried out from left to right in time, which re-solves the system on every interval of regularity. This yields wild solutions that are strong outside a closed set of times of arbitrarily small Hausdorff dimension. A causal mollification extends the construction to rough data, including every finite-energy velocity datum in dimensions two and three; in two dimensions the energy class is thus exactly the borderline of uniqueness. Finally, in three dimensions we construct Leray solutions satisfying the strong energy inequality and show that they are strong outside a closed set of times of vanishing $\mathcal H^{1/2}$ measure.
item.dc:creator: Xingyu Li

item.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.17625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.
item.dc:creator: Richard Duong, Janis Auffenberg, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: Geometric Partial Differential Equations of Hydrodynamic Type for Maps into F$_\text{man}$-Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.17653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a geometric framework for partial differential equations of hydrodynamic type on maps from a two-dimensional manifold into an F$_\text{man}$-Lie group. Using the left-invariant structure and the Maurer-Cartan form, we reduce these equations to non-linear evolution systems on the underlying F$_\text{man}$-algebra, governed by its Lie bracket and commutative associative product. We investigate the role of Poisson subalgebras, establishing that flatness of the canonical connection forces two-step nilpotency and yields a linearized evolution equation upon quotienting by the center. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a Poisson splitting and derive the corresponding tangential and transversal evolution equations. Under suitable reductivity assumptions, we show that their non-linear coupling is governed by the curvature of the canonical principal connection on the homogeneous space $G/H$. These results reveal the interplay between the algebraic structure of F$_\text{man}$-Lie groups and the geometric dynamics of hydrodynamic-type equations.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Casta\~neda-Montoya, Alexander Torres-Gomez

item.title: One-bubble stability, reduced coefficients, and threshold compactness for the Escobar functional
item.description: arXiv:2611.17750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact manifold with nonempty boundary and coercive conformal energy. For $n\ge5$, in a conformal representative with $H_g=0$, we prove quantitative stability near a concentrating boundary bubble whose center stays away from the umbilic locus. The norm of the constrained gradient controls the distance to the standard bubble family with sharp exponent $1/2$, and the distance to the Lyapunov--Schmidt corrected family linearly. In the same one-bubble neighborhood, at energies at least the sharp hemisphere value $S_\ast$, the distance to the standard family is also controlled linearly. These estimates follow from the exact reduced quadratic coefficient and the scale-derivative expansion of the reduced functional. The same scale equation shows that sequences of critical points at $S_\ast$ can concentrate only at umbilic points. For $n\ge3$, a profile decomposition without a sign assumption gives Palais--Smale compactness between $S_\ast$ and the first mixed level $(S_\ast^{n-1}+Y^{n-1})^{1/(n-1)}$, where $Y=C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)$, and this endpoint is sharp. Between $S_\ast$ and the two-bubble level, we characterize noncompact levels by the lower critical values. For $n\ge7$, we obtain the fourth-order reduced expansion at umbilic centers. Under local total umbilicity, we evaluate the correction exactly, determine the conformal weight of the reduced coefficient, and obtain the optimal algebraic comparison with the squared ambient Weyl norm.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: Contractions of realizations and differential invariants of the algebra sl(2,C)
item.description: arXiv:2611.17829v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincar\'e algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.
item.dc:creator: M. Staryi, M. Nesterenko

item.title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.17994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $\delta$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.
item.dc:creator: Jussi Behrndt, Badreddine Benhellal, Markus Holzmann, Konstantin Pankrashkin

item.title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.18247v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandra O. Vinnichenko

item.title: Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
item.description: arXiv:2611.18373v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. Integrating along a straight segment gives Guerra's sum rule, and dropping its remainder makes $u(0,\cdot)$ and $u(t,\cdot)$ an admissible pair for the dual Kantorovich problem with quadratic cost. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $\Lambda_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.
item.dc:creator: Elena Agliari, Adriano Barra, Andrea Ladiana, Andrea Lepre, Diego Pallara

item.title: Traveling waves of NLS system arising in optical material without Galilean symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2401.11683v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) system with cubic interactions arising in nonlinear optics, focusing on how the absence of Galilean symmetry affects solution dynamics. In the mass-critical case, we establish a new global existence result that contrasts with classical results. By exploiting the properties of traveling solitary waves, we obtain a condition on the initial data that relaxes the standard sharp assumptions. We also characterize the high-frequency limit of these traveling solitary waves as the frequency $\omega$ tends to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Li, Kai Wang, Qingxuan Wang

item.title: Information geometric regularization of unidimensional pressureless Euler equations yields global strong solutions
item.description: arXiv:2411.15121v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partial differential equations describing compressible fluids are prone to the formation of shock singularities, arising from faster upstream fluid particles catching up to slower, downstream ones. In geometric terms, this causes the deformation map to leave the manifold of diffeomorphisms. Information geometric regularization addresses this issue by changing the manifold geometry to make it geodesically complete. Empirical evidence suggests that this results in smooth solutions without adding artificial viscosity. This work makes a first step towards understanding this phenomenon rigorously, in the setting of the unidimensional pressureless Euler equations. It shows that their information geometric regularization has smooth global solutions. By establishing $\Gamma$-convergence of its variational description, it proves convergence of these solutions to entropy solutions of the nominal problem, in the limit of vanishing regularization parameter. A consequence of these results is that manifolds of unidimensional diffeomorphisms with information geometric regularization are geodesically complete.
item.dc:creator: Ruijia Cao, Florian Sch\"afer

item.title: Full range of infinite point blow-up exponents for the critical generalized KdV equation
item.description:
arXiv:2511.13538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the quintic, mass critical generalized Korteweg-de Vries equation, for any $
u \in ( rac{1}{2}, 1)$, we prove the existence of solutions in the energy space that blow up in finite time $T>0$ with the blow-up rate $\|\partial_x u(t)\|_{L^2} \sim (T-t)^{-
u}$ (infinite point blow-up). These solutions are constructed arbitrarily close to the family of solitons and correspond to the concentration of a soliton traveling at $+\infty$ in space as $t\uparrow T$. This complements the previous results obtained in the work of Martel, Merle, Rapha"el in 2015 on infinite point exotic blow-up, which were valid under the technical restriction $
u> rac {11}{13}$. The value $
u= rac 12$ corresponds to a critical case to be treated elsewhere. At the technical level, we implement a modification of the virial-energy functional, to allow all $
u >  rac 12$ and simplify the proof of energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Nailya Manatova

item.title: On the sharp multi-bubble stability for fractional Hardy--Sobolev equations: a quantitative approach in low dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2512.18350v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish sharp quantitative multi-bubble stability for nonnegative critical points of the fractional Hardy--Sobolev inequality in the low-dimensional regime $2s<N<6s-2t$. For functions whose energy is close to that of a finite superposition of bubbles, we prove that the Euler--Lagrange deficit controls linearly the distance, in the homogeneous fractional Sobolev norm, to the multi-bubble set, and we recover the precise bubble configuration. This yields quantitative rigidity under arbitrary finite weak interactions. The proof combines a localization scheme adapted to the Hardy weight, Kato--Ponce type weighted commutator estimates, a bubble-wise spectral gap inequality, and a sharp bubble-bubble interaction analysis. We also show that the linear rate is optimal by constructing a matching counterexample.
item.dc:creator: Souptik Chakraborty, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: Michael-Simon inequality for anisotropic energies close to the area via multilinear Kakeya-type bounds
item.description: arXiv:2601.10647v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an anisotropic integrand $F:\text{Gr}_k(\mathbb{R}^n)\to(0,\infty)$, we can generalize the classical isotropic area by looking at the functional $$\mathcal{F}(\Sigma^k):=\int_\Sigma F(T_x\Sigma)\,d\mathcal{H}^k.$$ While a monotonicity formula is not available for critical points, when $k=2$ and $n=3$ we show that the Michael-Simon inequality holds if $F$ is close to $1$ (in $C^1$), meaning that $\mathcal{F}$ is close to the usual area. Our argument is partly based on some key ideas of Almgren, who proved this result in an unpublished manuscript, but we largely simplify his original proof by showing a new functional inequality for vector fields on the plane, which can be seen as a quantitative version of Alberti's rank-one theorem, and we also remove a convexity assumption on $F$. As another byproduct, we also show Michael-Simon for another class of integrands which includes the $\ell^p$ norms for $p\in(1,\infty)$. For a general $F$ satisfying the atomic condition, we also show that the validity of Michael-Simon is equivalent to compactness of rectifiable varifolds.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Ars Inveniendi Analytica (2026), Paper No. 3, 33 pp
item.dc:creator: Guido De Philippis, Alessandro Pigati

item.title: Kinetic Fokker-Planck Equations with Nonlinear Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2607.00458v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study existence, regularity, and uniqueness for the nonlinear kinetic Fokker--Planck equation $$ \partial_t f=\Delta_v\Psi(f)-v\cdot\nabla_x f, \qquad f|_{t=0}=f_0, $$ on $\mathbb R^{2d}$. In the model case $\Psi(r)=r^s$, this equation couples nonlinear fast-diffusion/porous-medium type diffusion with kinetic transport. A distinctive feature is that the diffusion acts only in the velocity variable $v$, so that compactness in the spatial variable $x$ cannot be obtained from standard elliptic estimates and must instead be recovered through the hypoelliptic structure. Under general structural assumptions on $\Psi$, including the fast-diffusion powers $\Psi(r)=r^s$ with $s\in(0,1)$, we construct nonnegative weak solutions and prove quantitative anisotropic Besov regularity estimates. Under an additional mass-critical growth condition on the fast-diffusion side, the constructed weak solution preserves mass, admits a renormalized kinetic formulation, and is unique in the $L^1$-class of mass-preserving renormalized kinetic solutions. In the power-law case $\Psi(r)=r^s$, this condition is precisely $s\ge 1-1/d$ when $d\ge2$, while in dimension $d=1$ the whole fast-diffusion range $s\in(0,1)$ is covered. The main analytic ingredient is a parameter-dependent smoothing estimate for the kinetic semigroup generated by $$ \Psi'(\zeta)\Delta_v - v\cdot\nabla_x , $$ which quantitatively tracks the dependence on the kinetic level $\zeta$. Combined with the kinetic formulation, this estimate yields compactness in both spatial and velocity variables for the nonlinear hypoelliptic problem. As an application, we also obtain martingale-problem solutions to the associated distributional-density dependent stochastic differential equation.
item.dc:creator: Zimo Hao, Zhengyan Wu, Xicheng Zhang

item.title: Convergence for the porous medium equation with combustion in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2607.23429v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: \paper{Lou--Zhou}{JEMS}{2026} proved convergence and sharp threshold results for the one-dimensional porous medium equation with combustion reaction. In this paper, we extend these results to radially symmetric solutions with compactly supported initial data in higher dimensions. Under suitable assumptions on the reaction term, we first prove that every solution converges to a stationary solution. Based on this result, we obtain a spreading--transition--vanishing trichotomy with a sharp threshold. When $N=2$, transition solutions converge to the ignition temperature $\theta$ locally uniformly in $\mathbb R^2$ as $t\to\infty$. When $N\ge3$, they converge to positive ground state solutions uniformly in $\mathbb R^N$ as $t\to\infty$. The main difficulty is to exclude $\theta$ from the $\omega$-limit set when $N\ge3$. We prove this by normalizing the difference $u-\theta$, estimating the resulting limit with the heat kernel, and applying the radial zero number argument. In contrast, when $N=1$ or $N=2$, the $\omega$-limit set of a transition solution is $\{\theta\}$.
item.dc:creator: Maolin Zhou

item.title: Slowly travelling infinite point blow-up for the critical generalized KdV equation
item.description:
arXiv:2608.06585v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the finite time blow up phenomenon for the quintic, mass critical gKdV equation. We prove the existence of a class of solutions $U$ with infinite point, finite time blow up behavior, at the particular blow up rate $$\|\partial_x U(t)\|_{L^2} \sim (T-t)^{-
u}\quad 	ext{as} \quad t \uparrow T,$$ where $
u =  rac 12$, $T$ is the blow up time and where the travel speed of the blow up bubble is logarithmic. Therefore, we call this behaviour slowly travelling infinite point blow up. The special blow up rate $
u = rac 12$ is a threshold which separates finite and infinite point bubbling. In a previous work arXiv:2511.13538, the author constructed other infinite point blow up solutions for the continuum of rates $
u\in( rac 12,1)$, using polynomial tails in the space variable and extending the results in arXiv:1209.2510, restricted to $
u>  rac{11}{13}$. However, that work suggested a change of the tail for the threshold case. In the present paper, we consider an exponentially decaying tail on the right in space. As in arXiv:2511.13538, the initial data can be taken arbitrarily close to the ground state in $H^1$. From a technical perspective, in addition to the change of tail, we have to adapt the energy-virial functional to the presence of the exponential tail, by modifying a scaling term used to control the right-hand side of the blow up solution.
item.dc:creator: Nailya Manatova

item.title: Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold
item.description: arXiv:2609.01093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish local existence and uniqueness of solutions for the ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system posed on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$ and initial conditions given by a nonzero constant magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$ and arbitrary divergence-free velocity $v_0\in H^s$, in the range $(n+1)/2<s\le n/2+1$. The proof uses a Lagrangian wave--Hodge reformulation and exploits an Alfv\'en null--structure hidden in the pressure forcing. This work builds on Zhang \cite{Zhang2026} and provides a bridge from the Lagrangian theory to the Eulerian Cauchy problem. In particular, the constructed solutions are induced by a bi-Lipschitz and volume-preserving map.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Giardi

item.title: The $\alpha$-Limit Problem: Convergence of a Linear Degenerate Interface Transmission Problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.01237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the singular limit of a family of linear degenerate interface transmission problems arising from a regularization procedure in the newly proposed Two-Parameter Diffuse Domain Method (DDM2p). For $\alpha>0$, the regularized problem admits a strictly convex variational formulation on $H^{1}(\Omega)$. In the limit $\alpha\to0$, the problem degenerates to a weakly coupled interface system with a nonstandard energy structure. To characterize the limit, we introduce a closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal{H}\subset H^{1}(\Omega)$, defined through an auxiliary Helmholtz problem on an annular subdomain $\Omega_2\subset \Omega$, and identify the limiting energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ on $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that the regularized energies $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha}$ restricted to $\mathcal{H}$ $\Gamma$-converge to $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ in the strong $L^{2}(\Omega)$ topology, using the standard framework. Consequently, minimizers of $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha}$ converge to the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{E}_{0}$, which is shown to be equivalent to the solution of the limiting interface problem. We further prove a strong convergence $u_{\alpha}\to u_{0}$ in $H^{1}(\Omega)$ and establish a convergence rate of $O(\alpha)$. Numerical experiments in one spatial dimension exhibit first-order convergence, suggesting that the proved $O(\alpha)$ upper bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Toai Luong, Tadele Mengesha, Kerrek Stinson, Steven M. Wise, Ming Hei Wong

item.title: The periodic Wulff problem in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.06584v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize the minimizers of the anisotropic perimeter in the two-dimensional flat torus under an area constraint. We show that, as the prescribed area increases, global minimizers undergo two phase transitions, changing from a droplet (a rescaled Wulff shape) to a flat band wrapping around the torus in a preferred direction determined by the anisotropy (lamellar phase), and finally to a bubble (the complement of a reflected and rescaled Wulff shape). The transition thresholds are given explicitly in terms of the area and the lattice width of the Wulff shape. For certain non-symmetric surface tensions, the lamellar phase is absent altogether. Finally, we characterize the surface tensions for which further minimizers appear: this may happen only in the lamellar regime, and exactly when the Wulff shape has a corner whose normal cone contains, in its interior, a direction realizing the lattice width; in this case there are infinitely many minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Marco Bonacini, Alberto Fiorini

item.title: Open Inextensible Filaments in Planar Stokes Flow: Well-Posedness, Endpoint Asymptotics, and Straightening
item.description: arXiv:2609.10480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an inextensible open filament with free ends in a planar Stokes fluid. The system reduces to a third-order nonlocal curvature equation coupled to an elliptic equation for the tension. We prove local well-posedness for nearly critical initial data in supported Sobolev spaces $\widetilde H^s$, $-1/2<s\le0$, satisfying the arc-chord condition. For positive times, we prove improved Sobolev regularity and derive a $d^{3/2}$-type expansion at each free end using Wiener--Hopf factorization, where $d$ denotes the distance to that endpoint. We further prove global existence and exponential convergence to a straight filament for sufficiently small initial data and for finite-energy initial data satisfying $E(0)<\pi^2/4$. The finite-energy result follows from an energy identity and a geometric estimate relating the bending energy to the arc-chord constant. More generally, any finite-time breakdown must be accompanied by loss of the arc-chord condition, while every global solution either converges exponentially to a straight filament or has arc-chord constants tending to zero along a sequence of times tending to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Han Zhou

item.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.17712v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze resonance for partially dissipative systems, $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, where $A$ generates a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. {Resonance is} the phenomenon whereby a bounded, time-periodic $f$ yields an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, several other resonance notions, introduced here, may occur. Classically, {$T$-periodic solvability} is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-i\omega I)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces. The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.
item.dc:creator: Boris Muha, Sebastian Schwarzacher, Justin T. Webster

item.title: Regularity of critical immersions for scale-invariant curvature energies in even dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2609.39606v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For immersions of a closed $2h$-dimensional manifold $\Sigma$ into $\mathbb R^m$, we consider curvature energies that are invariant under ambient isometries and dilations, with the principal term $\int_{\Sigma} \big|\nabla^{(h-1)} \vec{\mathrm{I\!I}}\big|_g^2\,d\text{vol}_g$ and lower-order submanifold invariants. Following the four-dimensional approach developed in joint work with Bernard, Martino, and Rivi\`ere, we prove that every weak critical immersion in the natural Sobolev class $W^{h+1,2}$, whose induced metric and its inverse have $L^\infty$ coefficients, is real-analytic in harmonic coordinates. The proof combines geometric conservation laws, structural identities, and elliptic estimates with critical Sobolev coefficients to obtain Morrey decay and bootstrap to full regularity.
item.dc:creator: Tian Lan

item.title: An abstract averaging method for quasilinear equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.02155v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an abstract averaging method for equations $Mx=\varepsilon N(x,\varepsilon)$ in Banach spaces. The method applies when the equation can be separated into an averaged compatibility condition and a nonlinear complementary problem, and it allows the principal operator $M$ to be genuinely nonlinear. We prove that every nondegenerate zero of the corresponding averaged equation generates, for all sufficiently small nonzero values of $\varepsilon$, a nearby solution. Under a suitable small Lipschitz condition this solution is locally unique, while in the differentiable case it belongs to a unique local $C^1$ branch. The framework contains the abstract linear Fredholm averaging theory as a special case, but also covers quasilinear problems for which the principal operator has no invertible linearization at the reference state. We also determine the leading asymptotic profile of the solutions. Applications are given to a vector $p$-Laplacian Duffing system and to a nonsmooth problem in a Hilbert space.
item.dc:creator: Jean Mawhin, Jorge Novoa

item.title: Surface-to-Volume Homogenization of NonLinear Steklov Eigencouples with NonHomogeneous Orlicz Growth in Perforated Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.16693v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.
item.dc:creator: Hermann Douanla, Hubert Nnang, Joel Fotso Tachago, Jean Louis Woukeng

item.title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.24576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-\lambda u \quad \text{in }\Omega. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory. For $\lambda>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $\lambda$ and constant for sufficiently small $\lambda$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $\lambda\to+\infty$. In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(\Omega)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]
item.dc:creator: Annamaria Canino, Simone Mauro

item.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.06578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Xiuqing Chen, Ansgar J\"ungel, Mingyue Zhang

item.title: Heat kernel estimates for boundary traces of reflected diffusions on uniform domains
item.description: arXiv:2312.08546v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the boundary trace processes of reflected diffusions on uniform domains. We obtain stable-like heat kernel estimates for such a boundary trace process when the diffusion on the underlying ambient space satisfies sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates. Our arguments rely on new results of independent interest such as sharp two-sided estimates and the volume doubling property of the harmonic measure, the existence of a continuous extension of the Na\"im kernel to the topological boundary, and the Doob--Na\"im formula identifying the Dirichlet form of the boundary trace process as the pure-jump Dirichlet form whose jump kernel with respect to the harmonic measure is exactly (the continuous extension of) the Na\"im kernel.
item.dc:creator: Naotaka Kajino, Mathav Murugan

item.title: Transformation of Stochastic Recursions and Critical Phenomena in the Analysis of the Athreya-Aldous-Shields Cascade and Related Mean Flow Equations
item.description: arXiv:2411.00629v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the discounted branching random walk process introduced by Athreya (1985) and Aldous and Shields (1988), referred to as the Athreya-Aldous-Shields (AAS) cascade. This process can be viewed as an idealized version of the stochastic model introduced by Le Jan and Sznitman in 1997 for the Navier-Stokes equations. The AAS cascade exhibits phase transitions at the critical branching rates $\alpha=1$ and $\alpha=2$. These transitions are reflected in the behavior of the associated mean flow equation, a nonlocal ODE referred to as the $\alpha$-Riccati equation. It is known that if $\alpha>1$, the AAS cascade is explosive in the sense of infinitely many splittings in finite time, and the $\alpha$-Riccati equation has at least two solutions. In this paper, we establish finer structural properties of an explosive AAS cascade and obtain a stronger non-uniqueness result. Namely, for each initial data in a certain range, the $\alpha$-Riccati equation has an infinite family of distinct solutions parametrized by their convergence rates at infinity. Our approach exploits a simple transformation between the AAS cascade and its "linearized" counterpart, whose mean flow equation is precisely the well-studied pantograph equation. This transformation demonstrates how a relationship at the level of stochastic processes can reveal an otherwise hidden relationship at the level of mean flow equations.
item.dc:creator: Radu Dascaliuc, Tuan N. Pham, Enrique Thomann, Edward C. Waymire

item.title: Well-posedness for Wright--Fisher SPDEs with measurable drift
item.description: arXiv:2609.23518v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove weak existence and uniqueness in law of $[0,1]$-valued solutions for a class of scalar stochastic heat equations with measurable drifts $b : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, driven by Wright--Fisher noise. The only assumptions we require on the drift are Borel-measurability, and the one-way inequalities $-Cu\leq b(u)\leq C(1-u)$ for some $C<\infty$, compatible with the necessary condition $b(1)\leq 0\leq b(0)$. These are vastly more general conditions than were previously available. Our proof relies on a stochastic duality between the solution of the stochastic heat equation, and a voting scheme running along the graph of a branching-coalescing particle system, generalising the class of drifts for which a dual process is available. Our results and their proof put the regularisation-by-noise result of Barnes, Mytnik and Sun, and its explanation, on a much more general footing.
item.dc:creator: Jere Koskela, Oliver Tough

item.title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
item.description: arXiv:2610.22063v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Gobbert, Martin Kru\v{z}\'ik, Andreas Meister, Michael Muscedere
